summary: Configured PostgreSQL 16 streaming replication across node1 (primary), node2, and node3 (standbys) on CentOS Stream 10, secured entirely over TLS using a dedicated cluster CA. Generated a CA and per-node server certs plus a shared client cert (CN=replicator) on node1, distributed via SSH, and configured pg_hba.conf with hostssl+cert-only rules restricted to the three node IPs (non-SSL and non-CA-signed-cert replication attempts are rejected). Standbys were provisioned via pg_basebackup -R over sslmode=verify-full, confirmed streaming with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384 ciphers and cert auth, and validated with live data replication. Ran the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol (node2, node3, then node1) with boot-id proof of each restart and full data/replication recovery confirmed afterward, including a post-restart write propagating to both standbys.
actions_performed: Installed postgresql-server 16.14 on node1, node2, node3
Generated a self-signed CA (CN=pg-replication-ca) on node1, plus server certs for node1/node2/node3 (SAN=DNS+IP) and a shared client cert CN=replicator, all CA-signed
Set up passwordless root SSH between nodes using cluster-provided keys and distributed certs/keys to node2 and node3
Initialized node1 as primary (initdb), configured ssl=on with CA-verified certs, wal_level=replica, max_wal_senders/max_replication_slots
Rewrote pg_hba.conf on node1 to only allow hostssl replication with cert auth from the three cluster node IPs, and explicitly reject non-SSL replication attempts
Created replicator role (REPLICATION LOGIN, cert-authenticated, no password)
Opened firewalld port 5432/tcp permanently on all three nodes
Cloned node2 and node3 as standbys via pg_basebackup -R with sslmode=verify-full using the replicator client cert, auto-generating primary_conninfo with TLS
Configured TLS on node2/node3's own listeners (server cert + shared CA)
Verified streaming replication state (pg_stat_replication) and TLS cipher (pg_stat_ssl) on primary
Verified end-to-end data replication with a test table/insert visible on both standbys
Proved CA enforcement: a client cert not signed by the cluster CA was rejected with 'tlsv1 alert unknown ca'
Captured pre-restart boot_id and health/data baseline for all three nodes
Restarted node2, then node3, then node1 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling for exec availability and confirming changed boot_id after each
Verified post-restart recovery on each node: postgresql active, correct primary/standby role, data intact, and replication re-established with TLS
Performed a final post-restart write on the primary and confirmed it replicated to both standbys over TLS

evidence.summary: pg_basebackup cloned standbys with -R, both entered recovery mode, pg_stat_replication showed both streaming, and a test row inserted on node1 appeared on node2 and node3

evidence.requirement: Replication traffic carried over TLS using a cluster-created CA
evidence.summary: Self-signed CA generated on node1, server/client certs issued from it, and pg_stat_ssl confirmed both replication connections used TLS with TLS_AES_256_GCM_SHA384

evidence.requirement: Replication connections accepted only from peers presenting a CA-issued certificate
evidence.summary: pg_hba.conf restricted to hostssl+cert for replicator from the three node IPs with non-SSL replication rejected; a self-signed (non-CA) client cert was explicitly rejected with 'SSL error: tlsv1 alert unknown ca', while the CA-issued client cert succeeded

evidence.requirement: node2 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 21de1f79...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 1f5fe41f... with uptime 0 min; postgresql active, in recovery, data intact, and primary shows it streaming again

evidence.requirement: node3 restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id be303eb3...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to acf16532... with uptime 0 min; postgresql active, in recovery, data intact, and primary shows both standbys streaming again

evidence.requirement: node1 (primary) restart: healthy baseline, restart ack, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline boot_id 8f258838...; reboot acknowledged; boot_id changed to 61352ecb... with uptime 0 min; postgresql active and not in recovery (still primary), firewall rule persisted, both standbys reconnected via TLS streaming, and a post-restart insert propagated to both standbys
